answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties later verify and by staking tokens that are slashed when audits confirm fraud. A new identity starts with no history or stake, so splitting one attacker across a plume of accounts does not multiply its influence: each account must separately fund collateral and build trusted completions. An attacker must lock capital and pay the real cost of passing verification repeatedly; coordinated fake reviews risk losing the stake. The saffron island market can still be targeted, but identities alone buy no leverage.
